correctness.rationale: Polynomial exactness is necessary because the function class contains arbitrary degree-2 polynomials; with two points this forces ±h central differencing. Integral Taylor remainder is bounded by \(Mh^2/6\) and cubic f(u)=Mu³/6 attains equality. The prescribed Gaussian covariance gives the exact risk. Derivative signs reduce to \(x^6=\kappa q_\rho(x)\); \(6q_\rho-xq_\rho' > 0\), proved from \(6e^{2x}>6+7x+2x^2\), forces a unique global minimum. Uniform \(q_\rho(x)=(1-\rho)+\rho x+O(x^3)\) establishes two limiting exponents and the unique crossover \(z^6=z+\alpha,\ z\ge1\). verify.py is supplemental; finite mesh is not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A fixed two-query numerical differentiation experiment with spatially correlated errors is a natural setting in computer simulation and sensor calibration. The result classifies every finite-risk linear estimator, derives a unique exact global design for all covariance parameters, and locates the singular nugget boundary layer that changes the optimal small-noise exponent from 1/6 to 1/5. These structural and uniform asymptotic assertions are not the routine independent-noise bias–variance balancing formula; they give practical precision-selection guidance when errors share a mean-reverting component. Limit: two fixed linear queries with known parameters.
